subject.title: Feature request: Local plugin scanner CLI for pre-publish validation

question: Should ClawHub turn `clawhub package validate` into the supported pre-publish plugin scanner with redacted JSON/severity semantics, or keep it Plugin Inspector-only and design a separate scanner entrypoint?
rationale: The remaining work changes the public security-feedback contract for plugin authors and must decide which hosted scan signals can safely run locally and be exposed before publish.

options.title: Sponsor a supported scanner contract
options.body: Expand the author-facing CLI around `package validate` or a clearly named sibling command with shared deterministic checks, documented parity limits, redacted JSON output, and stable severity/exit behavior.

options.title: Keep validator-only scope
options.body: Document `package validate` as Plugin Inspector-only and leave hosted ClawScan results available only after publish or stored scan download.

options.title: Split a separate scanner design
options.body: Create a narrower follow-up spec for local scanner architecture before implementing any public CLI behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a supported scanner contract
recommendation.body: Expand the author-facing CLI around `package validate` or a clearly named sibling command with shared deterministic checks, documented parity limits, redacted JSON output, and stable severity/exit behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen owns the current package validation and scan command surface that any public scanner contract would likely extend or deliberately avoid.
